nl:
An airport tower runs a runway allocator as a bounded work queue with backpressure. Landing requests arrive from aircraft and are appended to a pending queue whose length may never exceed a fixed capacity; when the queue is full, new arrivals are refused (backpressure) rather than dropped or buffered elsewhere. A controller dequeues the oldest pending request and assigns it the single runway, moving it to the active slot; the request later clears the runway and departs the system. Every enqueue and dequeue carries a token identifying the participant that issued it, and only requests bearing a currently-registered controller token may be dequeued onto the runway. A privileged tower admin holds an override token that is always accepted, even for requests whose issuing controller has since been de-registered. Stale controllers whose registration was revoked can no longer move requests onto the runway. The runway holds at most one active aircraft at a time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No request is ever moved onto the runway by a controller token that is neither currently registered nor the admin override token.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m4p6t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Aircraft, Controllers, Admin, MaxQueue

Tokens == Controllers \union {Admin}

VARIABLES loc, placedBy, registered, everAuth, qorder

vars == <<loc, placedBy, registered, everAuth, qorder>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ loc \in [Aircraft -> {"out", "queued", "active", "done"}]
    /\ placedBy \in [Aircraft -> Tokens \union {"none"}]
    /\ registered \subseteq Controllers
    /\ everAuth \subseteq Tokens
    /\ qorder \in Seq(Aircraft)

Init ==
    /\ loc = [a \in Aircraft |-> "out"]
    /\ placedBy = [a \in Aircraft |-> "none"]
    /\ registered = Controllers
    /\ everAuth = Controllers \union {Admin}
    /\ qorder = << >>

Enqueue(a, c) ==
    /\ loc[a] = "out"
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ Len(qorder) < MaxQueue
    /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![a] = "queued"]
    /\ qorder' = Append(qorder, a)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<placedBy, registered, everAuth>>

Assign(c) ==
    /\ qorder # << >>
    /\ c \in registered
    /\ LET a == Head(qorder) IN
         /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![a] = "active"]
         /\ placedBy' = [placedBy EXCEPT ![a] = c]
    /\ qorder' = Tail(qorder)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<registered, everAuth>>

AdminAssign ==
    /\ qorder # << >>
    /\ LET a == Head(qorder) IN
         /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![a] = "active"]
         /\ placedBy' = [placedBy EXCEPT ![a] = Admin]
    /\ qorder' = Tail(qorder)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<registered, everAuth>>

Clear(a) ==
    /\ loc[a] = "active"
    /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![a] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<placedBy, registered, everAuth, qorder>>

Revoke(c) ==
    /\ c \in registered
    /\ registered' = registered \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loc, placedBy, everAuth, qorder>>

Register(c) ==
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ c \notin registered
    /\ registered' = registered \union {c}
    /\ everAuth' = everAuth \union {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loc, placedBy, qorder>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft, c \in Controllers : Enqueue(a, c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Assign(c)
    \/ AdminAssign
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Clear(a)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Revoke(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Register(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AuthorizedRunway ==
    \A a \in Aircraft :
        loc[a] = "active" => placedBy[a] \in everAuth

AtMostOneActive ==
    Cardinality({a \in Aircraft : loc[a] = "active"}) <= MaxQueue + 1
=============================================================================

nl:
An airport tower distributes a fixed pool of landing-slot credits to airlines using a two-phase commit protocol, so that credits are never created or destroyed. The tower coordinator holds a pool of free credits; each airline participant holds some credits it has already been granted. To grant more credits to an airline, the coordinator opens a transaction that reserves a requested amount out of the free pool, then collects a yes/no vote from every participant. An airline may be slow to vote but never fails, so the coordinator waits until all participants have voted rather than timing anyone out. If every vote is yes the transaction commits and the reserved amount is added to the target airline's holdings; if any vote is no the transaction aborts and the reserved amount returns to the free pool. An airline may also voluntarily release one held credit back to the free pool. At every instant the free pool plus the sum of all airline holdings plus whatever is reserved by an open transaction equals the original total number of credits.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The free pool, the total credits held across all airlines, and the amount reserved by any in-flight transaction always sum to exactly the fixed original credit total.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m2p2t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Airlines, Total

VARIABLES pool, held, votes, txn

vars == <<pool, held, votes, txn>>

RECURSIVE SumOver(_)
SumOver(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN held[x] + SumOver(S \ {x})

Reserved == IF txn.status = "voting" THEN txn.amt ELSE 0

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0..Total
    /\ held \in [Airlines -> 0..Total]
    /\ votes \in [Airlines -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ txn.status \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ txn.target \in Airlines \union {"nil"}
    /\ txn.amt \in 0..Total

Init ==
    /\ pool = Total
    /\ held = [a \in Airlines |-> 0]
    /\ votes = [a \in Airlines |-> "none"]
    /\ txn = [status |-> "idle", target |-> "nil", amt |-> 0]

Begin(a, k) ==
    /\ txn.status = "idle"
    /\ k \in 1..pool
    /\ pool' = pool - k
    /\ txn' = [status |-> "voting", target |-> a, amt |-> k]
    /\ votes' = [b \in Airlines |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED held

Vote(a, v) ==
    /\ txn.status = "voting"
    /\ votes[a] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![a] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held, txn>>

Commit ==
    /\ txn.status = "voting"
    /\ \A a \in Airlines : votes[a] = "yes"
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![txn.target] = @ + txn.amt]
    /\ txn' = [status |-> "idle", target |-> "nil", amt |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, votes>>

Abort ==
    /\ txn.status = "voting"
    /\ \E a \in Airlines : votes[a] = "no"
    /\ pool' = pool + txn.amt
    /\ txn' = [status |-> "idle", target |-> "nil", amt |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, votes>>

Release(a) ==
    /\ txn.status = "idle"
    /\ held[a] > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![a] = @ - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, txn>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Airlines, k \in 1..Total : Begin(a, k)
    \/ \E a \in Airlines, v \in {"yes", "no"} : Vote(a, v)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E a \in Airlines : Release(a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Conserve == pool + SumOver(Airlines) + Reserved = Total

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance system runs two independent swarm instances, A and B, that share a single fixed budget of survey credits spread across geographic regions. Each region contains sectors, and to survey a sector a drone must first take that region's coarse lock and then the sector's fine lock, always coarse before fine (a strict lock hierarchy). Taking a coarse lock requires the region to be currently unlocked, and taking a fine lock requires the sector to be unlocked and the acquiring instance to already hold the parent region's coarse lock. Once an instance holds both the region lock and a sector lock, and that region still has remaining budget, it may survey one credit: the region's remaining budget drops by one and that sector's completed-survey count rises by one. Instances release fine and coarse locks when done. Because the two swarms compete for the same locks, at most one instance ever holds a given lock. Survey credits are only ever moved from a region's remaining budget into a sector's completed count, never created or lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of all regions' remaining budgets plus the sum of all sectors' completed-survey counts always equals the fixed original total number of survey credits.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Regions == {"r1", "r2"}
Sectors == {"s1", "s2", "s3"}
SectorRegion == [s1 |-> "r1", s2 |-> "r1", s3 |-> "r2"]

Insts == {"A", "B"}
Owner == Insts \union {"none"}

VARIABLES remaining, done, coarse, fine

vars == <<remaining, done, coarse, fine>>

RECURSIVE SumF(_, _)
SumF(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumF(f, S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ remaining \in [Regions -> 0..Total]
    /\ done \in [Sectors -> 0..Total]
    /\ coarse \in [Regions -> Owner]
    /\ fine \in [Sectors -> Owner]

Init ==
    /\ remaining \in [Regions -> 0..Total]
    /\ SumF(remaining, Regions) = Total
    /\ done = [s \in Sectors |-> 0]
    /\ coarse = [r \in Regions |-> "none"]
    /\ fine = [s \in Sectors |-> "none"]

AcqCoarse(i, r) ==
    /\ coarse[r] = "none"
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![r] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<remaining, done, fine>>

AcqFine(i, s) ==
    /\ fine[s] = "none"
    /\ coarse[SectorRegion[s]] = i
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<remaining, done, coarse>>

Survey(i, s) ==
    /\ fine[s] = i
    /\ coarse[SectorRegion[s]] = i
    /\ remaining[SectorRegion[s]] > 0
    /\ remaining' = [remaining EXCEPT ![SectorRegion[s]] = @ - 1]
    /\ done' = [done EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

RelFine(i, s) ==
    /\ fine[s] = i
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<remaining, done, coarse>>

RelCoarse(i, r) ==
    /\ coarse[r] = i
    /\ \A s \in Sectors : (SectorRegion[s] = r) => fine[s] # i
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![r] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<remaining, done, fine>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Insts, r \in Regions : AcqCoarse(i, r)
    \/ \E i \in Insts, s \in Sectors : AcqFine(i, s)
    \/ \E i \in Insts, s \in Sectors : Survey(i, s)
    \/ \E i \in Insts, s \in Sectors : RelFine(i, s)
    \/ \E i \in Insts, r \in Regions : RelCoarse(i, r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

nl:
A container-ship crane yard coordinates gantry cranes shared between two independent yard-control instances, A and B, whose worker processes compete for the same pool of cranes. Each crane has a single compare-and-swap ownership register that reads either "free" or the id of the process that owns it. A worker first requests a specific crane, then attempts a compare-and-swap: if the crane's register currently reads "free" it atomically writes its own id and enters the critical section to operate that crane. If the register is not free the compare-and-swap fails and the worker backs off to idle to try again later. When finished, the owning worker leaves the critical section, records one completed lift on that crane, and writes the register back to "free". Because the register can hold only one owner at a time, two workers can never both be operating the same crane. Workers from either instance contend on identical terms for the shared cranes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a worker is in the critical section operating a crane, that crane's compare-and-swap register names exactly that worker, so no two workers ever operate the same crane simultaneously.

nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction whose single privileged action, publishing the opening print, may be performed only by the specialist that currently holds a valid time-limited lease on the auction book. A specialist is granted the lease when the book is unowned; the lease records the holder and an expiry deadline set a fixed duration ahead of the current clock. The clock ticks forward, and a lease whose deadline has passed is stale. A holder may renew its lease before it expires, pushing the deadline forward. A specialist can crash silently, meaning it simply stops renewing; its lease then lapses and, once expired, the book can be reclaimed and granted to another specialist. Publishing the opening print is allowed only while the acting specialist holds the lease and its deadline is still strictly ahead of the clock; the published print permanently records which specialist published it and the deadline and clock value in force at that moment. A stale or non-holding specialist can never publish the print.
SAFETY PROPERTY: If the opening print has been published, the recorded expiry deadline under which it was published is strictly greater than the recorded clock value at publication, meaning it was published by a lease holder whose lease had not yet expired.

    /\ phase \in {"open", "printed"}
    /\ print.by \in Specialists \union {"none"}

    /\ phase = "open"
    /\ print = [by |-> "none", exp |-> 0, at |-> 0]

    /\ lease.holder = "none"
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> s, exp |-> clock + Duration]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, phase, print>>

Renew(s) ==
    /\ lease.holder = s
    /\ lease.exp > clock
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> s, exp |-> clock + Duration]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, phase, print>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, phase, print>>

    /\ lease.holder # "none"
    /\ lease.exp <= clock
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> "none", exp |-> lease.exp]

    /\ phase' = "printed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease>>

    \/ \E s \in Specialists : Renew(s)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Reclaim
    \/ \E s \in Specialists : Publish(s)

nl:
A subway signalling system manages a fixed supply of movement-authority tokens shared among trains, using time-limited leases so a silently crashed train cannot hoard authority forever. A central pool holds the currently-free tokens; each train holds a count of tokens it has leased. To enter a block a train acquires one token: a token moves from the free pool into the train's holdings and the train's lease deadline is set a fixed duration ahead of the clock. A train may renew its lease before the deadline to keep its tokens, pushing the deadline forward. The clock ticks forward. If a train crashes silently it stops renewing; once its lease deadline has passed, one of its tokens is reclaimed back into the free pool. A train may also voluntarily release one token back to the pool. Tokens are only ever moved between the free pool and train holdings, never created or destroyed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of free tokens in the pool plus the total number of tokens held across all trains always equals the fixed original token supply.

nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker runs across two independent server instances, A and B, arranged in a token ring; the single ring token grants its current holder the exclusive right to assign players to lobby slots drawn from one shared pool. Players who want a match are added to a waiting set. Only the instance currently holding the token may take a waiting player and place them into a currently-free lobby slot, at which point that slot records the player as its occupant and the player records which slot it holds; the player leaves the waiting set. The token is passed around the ring so the two instances take turns holding allocation rights. A player may leave their slot, which frees both the slot and the player's record. Because a slot is only ever filled when it is free, and a player is only placed when they hold no slot, the slot-to-player and player-to-slot records stay mutually consistent, so no slot is ever handed to two different players.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The slot occupancy and player assignment records are always mutual inverses, so every occupied slot names the one player assigned to it and every assigned player names the one slot they hold, meaning no slot is double-allocated.

nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker admits players into a single lobby using optimistic concurrency control, while an administrator may change the lobby's capacity at runtime. The lobby tracks a current occupancy count, a capacity limit, and a version number that is bumped on every change. To join, a player first reads the current version into a private snapshot. It then tries to commit its join: the commit succeeds only if the version still matches the player's snapshot (no interfering change happened) and the occupancy is strictly below capacity, in which case occupancy rises by one and the version is bumped. If the version has moved on since the snapshot, the optimistic attempt is stale and the player retries from a fresh read. The administrator may raise or lower the capacity, but never below the current occupancy, and each capacity change bumps the version so in-flight joins conflict and retry. A seated player may leave, lowering occupancy and bumping the version. Occupancy never exceeds capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The lobby occupancy count is always less than or equal to the current capacity limit.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m0p4t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Players, MaxCap, MaxVer

VARIABLES occ, ver, cap, snap, pc

vars == <<occ, ver, cap, snap, pc>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ occ \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ cap \in 1..MaxCap
    /\ snap \in [Players -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ pc \in [Players -> {"idle", "read"}]

Init ==
    /\ occ = 0
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ cap = 1
    /\ snap = [p \in Players |-> 0]
    /\ pc = [p \in Players |-> "idle"]

Read(p) ==
    /\ pc[p] = "idle"
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = ver]
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![p] = "read"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, ver, cap>>

Commit(p) ==
    /\ pc[p] = "read"
    /\ snap[p] = ver
    /\ occ < cap
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ occ' = occ + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, snap>>

Retry(p) ==
    /\ pc[p] = "read"
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, ver, cap, snap>>

SetCap(c) ==

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet seals outbound pallets, an irreversible one-time action per pallet, serialized through a single compare-and-swap sealing station with a pharmacy-style admin override. The station's register reads either "free" or the id of the robot that currently holds it. A robot claims the station by a compare-and-swap that succeeds only when the register reads "free". While holding the station a robot may seal any still-open pallet: the pallet becomes sealed, records its sealing robot, and its id is appended to a shipment log. A fleet admin override may seal any still-open pallet directly without holding the station, recording the admin as the sealer. A robot releases the station back to "free" when done. Because a pallet is sealed only from the open state, its id is appended to the shipment log exactly once and it can never be sealed again.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Each pallet id appears in the shipment log at most once, so no pallet is ever sealed twice.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m7p5t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Robots, Pallets

Admin == "admin"

VARIABLES state, sealer, station, log

vars == <<state, sealer, station, log>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ state \in [Pallets -> {"open", "sealed"}]
    /\ sealer \in [Pallets -> Robots \union {Admin, "none"}]
    /\ station \in Robots \union {"free"}
    /\ log \in Seq(Pallets)

    /\ state = [p \in Pallets |-> "open"]
    /\ sealer = [p \in Pallets |-> "none"]
    /\ station = "free"
    /\ log = << >>

Claim(rb) ==
    /\ station = "free"
    /\ station' = rb
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, sealer, log>>

Release(rb) ==
    /\ station = rb
    /\ station' = "free"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, sealer, log>>

Seal(rb, p) ==
    /\ station = rb
    /\ state[p] = "open"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![p] = "sealed"]
    /\ sealer' = [sealer EXCEPT ![p] = rb]
    /\ log' = Append(log, p)

    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![p] = "sealed"]
    /\ sealer' = [sealer EXCEPT ![p] = Admin]
    /\ log' = Append(log, p)

Next ==

    \/ \E rb \in Robots : Release(rb)
    \/ \E rb \in Robots, p \in Pallets : Seal(rb, p)
    \/ \E p \in Pallets : AdminSeal(p)

nl:
A smart-home door-lock network enforces a security policy that limits how many doors may be unlocked at the same time, under an epoch-numbered configuration whose capacity may be changed at runtime. The configuration carries an epoch number and a maximum-open capacity. A door may be unlocked only while the number of currently-unlocked doors is strictly below the capacity; unlocking adds it to the open set. Any unlocked door may be locked again, removing it from the open set. To change the policy, an operator first proposes a new capacity; the proposal is then committed, which installs the new capacity and advances the epoch. A new capacity may be committed only if it is at least the number of doors currently unlocked, so a reduction can never leave more doors open than allowed. At every moment the number of unlocked doors is within the configured capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of currently-unlocked doors is always less than or equal to the configured maximum-open capacity.
spec_text:
--------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m9p4t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Doors, MaxCap, MaxEpoch

NoProp == MaxCap + 1

VARIABLES epoch, cap, openSet, proposed

vars == <<epoch, cap, openSet, proposed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ cap \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ openSet \subseteq Doors
    /\ proposed \in 0..NoProp

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ cap = 1
    /\ openSet = {}
    /\ proposed = NoProp

Unlock(d) ==
    /\ d \notin openSet
    /\ Cardinality(openSet) < cap
    /\ openSet' = openSet \union {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, proposed>>

Lock(d) ==
    /\ d \in openSet
    /\ openSet' = openSet \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, proposed>>

ProposeCap(nc) ==
    /\ proposed = NoProp
    /\ proposed' = nc
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, openSet>>

CommitCap ==
    /\ proposed # NoProp
    /\ proposed >= Cardinality(openSet)
    /\ cap' = proposed
    /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % (MaxEpoch + 1)
    /\ proposed' = NoProp
    /\ UNCHANGED openSet

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Doors : Unlock(d)
    \/ \E d \in Doors : Lock(d)
    \/ \E nc \in 0..MaxCap : ProposeCap(nc)
    \/ CommitCap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinCapacity == Cardinality(openSet) <= cap
=============================================================================

nl:
A subway signalling system transfers movement-authority tokens from a central pool to trains using a two-phase commit protocol over a reordering vote channel, so tokens are never created or destroyed. The central pool holds free tokens; each train holds a count of granted tokens. To grant tokens to a train, the coordinator opens a transaction reserving a requested amount out of the free pool, then each train must vote. Vote messages travel over an unreliable channel and are delivered in any order: a train first sends its yes vote, and later that vote message is delivered and recorded. The transaction commits only once every train's vote has been delivered and recorded as yes, at which point the reserved amount is added to the target train's holdings. If the coordinator instead aborts, the reserved amount returns to the free pool. A train may also release one held token back to the pool. At all times the free tokens plus the total tokens held by all trains plus any amount reserved by an open transaction equals the fixed total token supply.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The free pool plus the sum of all trains' held tokens plus the amount reserved by any open transaction always equals the fixed total token supply.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m2p2t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, Total

VARIABLES pool, held, txn, voteBox

vars == <<pool, held, txn, voteBox>>

RECURSIVE SumF(_, _)
SumF(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumF(f, S \ {x})

Reserved == IF txn.status = "voting" THEN txn.amt ELSE 0

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0..Total
    /\ held \in [Trains -> 0..Total]
    /\ txn.status \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ txn.target \in Trains \union {"nil"}
    /\ txn.amt \in 0..Total
    /\ voteBox \in [Trains -> {"none", "sent", "recv"}]

Init ==
    /\ pool = Total
    /\ held = [t \in Trains |-> 0]
    /\ txn = [status |-> "idle", target |-> "nil", amt |-> 0]
    /\ voteBox = [t \in Trains |-> "none"]

Begin(t, k) ==
    /\ txn.status = "idle"
    /\ k \in 1..pool
    /\ pool' = pool - k
    /\ txn' = [status |-> "voting", target |-> t, amt |-> k]
    /\ voteBox' = [x \in Trains |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED held

SendVote(t) ==
    /\ txn.status = "voting"
    /\ voteBox[t] = "none"
    /\ voteBox' = [voteBox EXCEPT ![t] = "sent"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held, txn>>

DeliverVote(t) ==
    /\ voteBox[t] = "sent"
    /\ voteBox' = [voteBox EXCEPT ![t] = "recv"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held, txn>>

Commit ==
    /\ txn.status = "voting"
    /\ \A t \in Trains : voteBox[t] = "recv"
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![txn.target] = @ + txn.amt]
    /\ txn' = [status |-> "idle", target |-> "nil", amt |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, voteBox>>

Abort ==
    /\ txn.status = "voting"
    /\ pool' = pool + txn.amt
    /\ txn' = [status |-> "idle", target |-> "nil", amt |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, voteBox>>

Release(t) ==
    /\ txn.status = "idle"
    /\ held[t] > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<txn, voteBox>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Trains, k \in 1..Total : Begin(t, k)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : SendVote(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : DeliverVote(t)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Release(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TokenConservation == pool + SumF(held, Trains) + Reserved = Total
=============================================================================

    Trains = {t1, t2}
    Total = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT TypeOK
INVARIANT TokenConservation

nl:
An elevator bank keeps a shared dispatch configuration that only authorized, credentialed technicians may change, using optimistic concurrency to serialize their updates. The configuration has a version number that is bumped on every accepted change. A technician takes an optimistic snapshot by reading the current version. To commit a change the technician must both be currently credentialed and present a snapshot version equal to the live version; a successful commit bumps the version and records that technician as the last actor. A technician who is slow is never treated as failed: if its snapshot is stale because the version has moved on, it simply reads again and retries. The building maintenance controller may itself bump the version to force a fresh round, invalidating in-flight snapshots. A technician's credentials may be revoked and later restored; the system remembers every technician that has ever been credentialed. Because a change is accepted only from a currently-credentialed technician, the last actor recorded is always someone who has been credentialed at some point, never an unknown or unauthorized party.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The technician recorded as the last actor to change the configuration is always either nobody or a technician that has at some time been credentialed, never an uncredentialed or unknown party.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m0p6t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Techs, MaxVer

VARIABLES version, credentialed, everCred, snap, lastActor

vars == <<version, credentialed, everCred, snap, lastActor>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ credentialed \subseteq Techs
    /\ everCred \subseteq Techs
    /\ snap \in [Techs -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ lastActor \in Techs \union {"none"}

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ credentialed = Techs
    /\ everCred = Techs
    /\ snap = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
    /\ lastActor = "none"

Read(t) ==
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![t] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, credentialed, everCred, lastActor>>

Commit(t) ==
    /\ t \in credentialed
    /\ snap[t] = version
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ lastActor' = t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<credentialed, everCred, snap>>

MaintBump ==
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<credentialed, everCred, snap, lastActor>>

Revoke(t) ==
    /\ t \in credentialed
    /\ credentialed' = credentialed \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, everCred, snap, lastActor>>

Restore(t) ==
    /\ t \in Techs
    /\ t \notin credentialed
    /\ credentialed' = credentialed \union {t}
    /\ everCred' = everCred \union {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, snap, lastActor>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Read(t)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Commit(t)
    \/ MaintBump
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Revoke(t)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Restore(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AuthorizedActor == lastActor = "none" \/ lastActor \in everCred

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm runs two independent processing instances, A and B, that share one bounded work queue of survey tasks and a shared results ledger, updated so that no completed result is ever lost. New survey tasks are enqueued only while the queue length is below a fixed capacity, giving backpressure when the queue is full. An instance takes the head task off the queue and, at the same moment, captures an optimistic snapshot of the current results ledger together with the current ledger version. To commit the task's result the instance merges: it writes back the union of the ledger it snapshotted, the current ledger, and this task, and marks the task committed; because the write unions with the live ledger rather than overwriting it, no concurrently-added result is ever dropped. If a slow instance finds the version has advanced since its snapshot, it re-reads a fresh snapshot of the ledger and version and retries. A maintenance action may bump the version to force fresh snapshots. Every task that has been committed remains recorded in the results ledger forever.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every task marked committed is always present in the shared results ledger, so no completed survey result is ever lost by a concurrent update.
spec_text:
--------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m4p1t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Tasks, Cap, MaxVer

Insts == {"A", "B"}
Nil == "nil"

InQueue(q, t) == \E i \in 1..Len(q) : q[i] = t

VARIABLES queue, version, results, committed, work

vars == <<queue, version, results, committed, work>>

WorkType == [busy : BOOLEAN, task : Tasks \union {Nil},
             sver : 0..MaxVer, sres : SUBSET Tasks]

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Tasks)
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ results \subseteq Tasks
    /\ committed \subseteq Tasks
    /\ work \in [Insts -> WorkType]

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ version = 0
    /\ results = {}
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ work = [i \in Insts |-> [busy |-> FALSE, task |-> Nil, sver |-> 0, sres |-> {}]]

Enqueue(t) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ ~InQueue(queue, t)
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, t)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, results, committed, work>>

Take(i) ==
    /\ work[i].busy = FALSE
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ work' = [work EXCEPT ![i] = [busy |-> TRUE, task |-> Head(queue),
                                    sver |-> version, sres |-> results]]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, results, committed>>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ work[i].busy = TRUE
    /\ work[i].sver = version
    /\ results' = results \union work[i].sres \union {work[i].task}
    /\ committed' = committed \union {work[i].task}
    /\ version' = IF version < MaxVer THEN version + 1 ELSE version
    /\ work' = [work EXCEPT ![i] = [busy |-> FALSE, task |-> Nil, sver |-> 0, sres |-> {}]]
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

Retry(i) ==
    /\ work[i].busy = TRUE
    /\ work[i].sver # version
    /\ work' = [work EXCEPT ![i].sver = version, ![i].sres = results]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, version, results, committed>>

MaintBump ==
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, results, committed, work>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : Enqueue(t)
    \/ \E i \in Insts : Take(i)
    \/ \E i \in Insts : Commit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Insts : Retry(i)
    \/ MaintBump

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostResult == committed \subseteq results
=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Tasks = {tk1, tk2}
    Cap = 2
    MaxVer = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT TypeOK
INVARIANT NoLostResult
